evals.name: deal-objections-eval-1-tool-mandate
evals.prompt: with zime-mcp connected, user asks: 'What objections have come up in the Swisscom deal?' — earlier in this conversation a recap already mentioned two objections from one call
evals.expected_output: The skill calls get_deal_objections with query 'Swisscom' rather than answering from the two objections already in chat context — the tool covers every call and CRM record in the deal, which the chat does not. No deal_id is passed since none is known. The returned objections keep their severity and addressed/unaddressed status, with open objections led first.
expectations: get_deal_objections is called even though partial objection data exists in chat context
The query contains only deal/company words and no deal_id is invented
Severity and addressed/unaddressed status from the tool are preserved per objection
Open (unaddressed) objections are presented before addressed ones

evals.name: deal-objections-eval-2-disambiguation
evals.prompt: the tool returns multiple_matches with three deal candidates (name, account, stage, last-call date); the user picks the second
evals.expected_output: The skill shows all three candidates with their name, account, stage, and last-call date, asks which deal the user means, and re-calls with the chosen candidate's deal_id. No objection content is produced while the deal is unresolved.
expectations: All candidates are shown with name, account, stage, and last-call date
The user's choice is passed back as deal_id on the second call
No objection list is generated before the deal is resolved

evals.name: deal-objections-eval-3-honest-failure
evals.prompt: get_deal_objections errors with {"error":"FORBIDDEN"} on both the first attempt and the retry
evals.expected_output: After one retry the skill states the deal isn't accessible to this user or the service refused the request, without inventing an objection list from memory and without leaking backend detail beyond the clean code's meaning.
expectations: The tool call is retried exactly once
FORBIDDEN is explained as an access refusal in plain language
No from-memory objection list is substituted after the failure
